title: Staging to Production Deploy Issues
description: Fix problems pushing staging changes to production — database sync, URL mismatches, cache, and lost content conflicts.

steps.title: Define Deploy Scope and Rollback Plan
steps.instructions: Document what is being deployed: code only, database only, or both. Take full production backup before any push. Define rollback steps and time window.

steps.title: Deploy Code Changes First
steps.instructions: Push theme, plugin, and mu-plugin file changes via git, SFTP, or host deploy tool. Do not overwrite production wp-config.php or uploads without intent.

steps.title: Use Selective Database Sync
steps.instructions: Never blindly import full staging DB to production — it overwrites live orders, users, and content. Sync only specific tables or use migration tools with exclude rules.

steps.title: Run Production URL Search-Replace
steps.instructions: If staging URLs exist in deployed data, run serialization-safe replace from staging.domain to production.domain on production after import.

steps.title: Exclude Sensitive Options from Sync
steps.instructions: Do not overwrite siteurl, home, SMTP credentials, API keys, or analytics IDs. Maintain a list of options to exclude per client environment.

steps.title: Flush All Caches After Deploy
steps.instructions: Purge page cache, object cache, CDN, and opcode cache. Regenerate Elementor/CSS caches if applicable. Test in incognito.

steps.title: Verify Production Integrations
steps.instructions: Confirm live payment gateways, SMTP, analytics, and CRM connections still use production credentials — not staging test keys.

steps.title: Run Production Smoke Test
steps.instructions: Test homepage, checkout, forms, login, and key client workflows. Monitor error logs for 24 hours post-deploy. Document deploy in client changelog.
